title: OSHA general industry exit routes and emergency planning practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry practice questions on exit routes, emergency action plans and fire prevention plans (29 CFR 1910 Subpart E), each linked to its rule.

questions.question: Under the 1910.34(c) definition of self-luminous, which of these is given as an example of a self-contained power source?

options.A: Batteries
options.B: Tritium
options.C: The building's electrical service
options.D: Daylight from nearby windows

questions.explanation: Self-luminous means "a light source that is illuminated by a self-contained power source (e.g., tritium) and that operates independently from external power sources." The definition adds that batteries are not acceptable self-contained power sources.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.34, Coverage and definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Sections 1910.34 through 1910.39 apply to workplaces in general industry, except which workplaces?

options.A: Workplaces with 10 or fewer employees
options.B: One-story buildings
options.C: Office buildings
options.D: Mobile workplaces such as vehicles or vessels

questions.explanation: These sections "apply to workplaces in general industry except mobile workplaces such as vehicles or vessels."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.34, Coverage and definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.36(a)(3) require of each fire door that protects an opening into an exit, including its frame and hardware?

options.A: It must be listed or approved by a nationally recognized testing laboratory
options.B: It must be painted red
options.C: It must be inspected by the local fire marshal every month
options.D: It must be at least 3 inches thick

questions.explanation: The rule says "Each fire door, including its frame and hardware, must be listed or approved by a nationally recognized testing laboratory."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Exit stairs continue past the level on which the exit discharge is located. What does 1910.36(c)(3) require at that level?

options.A: Nothing, as long as the stairs are lighted
options.B: A ramp in place of the lower flight
options.C: Doors, partitions, or other effective means that interrupt the stairs and clearly indicate the direction of travel leading to the exit discharge
options.D: A handrail extension, with nothing else

questions.explanation: Such exit stairs "must be interrupted at that level by doors, partitions, or other effective means that clearly indicate the direction of travel leading to the exit discharge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An opening into an exit must be protected by what?

options.A: A fabric curtain
options.B: A door propped open with a wedge
options.C: A sliding screen
options.D: A self-closing fire door that remains closed or automatically closes in an emergency

questions.explanation: "An opening into an exit must be protected by a self-closing fire door that remains closed or automatically closes in an emergency upon the sounding of a fire alarm or employee alarm system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.36(d)(2) say about devices and alarms on exit route doors?

options.A: The doors must be free of any device or alarm that could restrict emergency use of the exit route if the device or alarm fails
options.B: Every exit route door must have an alarm that locks the door when it sounds
options.C: A device may restrict use of the exit route if it is tested monthly
options.D: Alarms may be fitted only to doors on the ground floor

questions.explanation: The rule says "Exit route doors must be free of any device or alarm that could restrict emergency use of the exit route if the device or alarm fails."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A storage room used by 12 workers holds contents that are likely to burn with extreme rapidity. How must the side-hinged door connecting it to an exit route swing?

options.A: In either direction, because fewer than 50 people occupy the room
options.B: Inward, to keep a fire inside the room
options.C: Out in the direction of exit travel, because the room is a high hazard area
options.D: In either direction, as long as the door is side-hinged

questions.explanation: The door "must swing out in the direction of exit travel if the room is designed to be occupied by more than 50 people or if the room is a high hazard area (i.e., contains contents that are likely to burn with extreme rapidity or explode)." The high hazard condition applies whatever the number of occupants.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where does 1910.36 permit an exit route door to be locked from the inside?

options.A: In warehouses after business hours
options.B: Only in mental, penal or correctional facilities, with supervisory personnel continuously on duty and an evacuation plan
options.C: In retail stores at night
options.D: In any building with a security guard at the entrance

questions.explanation: An exit route door may be locked from the inside "only in mental, penal, or correctional facilities and then only if supervisory personnel are continuously on duty and the employer has a plan to remove occupants from the facility during an emergency."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Exit route capacity, height and width
questions.question: What does 1910.36(f)(2) say about the capacity of an exit route along the way to the exit discharge?

options.A: It may decrease by up to half
options.B: It must double at each floor
options.C: It may decrease once the route passes the first fire door
options.D: It may not decrease in the direction of exit route travel to the exit discharge

questions.explanation: The rule says "The capacity of an exit route may not decrease in the direction of exit route travel to the exit discharge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Exit route capacity, height and width
questions.question: Where only one exit access leads to an exit or exit discharge, how wide does 1910.36(g)(2) require the exit and exit discharge to be?

options.A: At least half the width of the exit access
options.B: At least equal to the width of the exit access
options.C: At least 22 inches, whatever the exit access width
options.D: Exactly 36 inches

questions.explanation: "Where there is only one exit access leading to an exit or exit discharge, the width of the exit and exit discharge must be at least equal to the width of the exit access."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Exit route capacity, height and width
questions.question: An outdoor exit route must not have a dead-end longer than how many feet?

options.A: 20 feet (6.2 m)
options.B: 50 feet
options.C: 75 feet
options.D: 100 feet

questions.explanation: "The outdoor exit route must not have a dead-end that is longer than 20 feet (6.2 m)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.37(a)(3), which way may an exit access not go to reach an exit or exit discharge?

options.A: Along a corridor
options.B: Down a ramp where the exit route is not substantially level
options.C: Through a room that can be locked, such as a bathroom
options.D: Past a doorway marked "Not an Exit"

questions.explanation: The rule says "The exit access must not go through a room that can be locked, such as a bathroom, to reach an exit or exit discharge, nor may it lead into a dead-end corridor." It also requires stairs or a ramp where the route is not substantially level.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.37(e), when is an employer excused from installing and maintaining an operable employee alarm system?

options.A: When the workplace has 10 or fewer employees
options.B: When the building has an automatic sprinkler system
options.C: When every exit is marked with an EXIT sign
options.D: When employees can promptly see or smell a fire or other hazard in time to provide adequate warning to them

questions.explanation: Employers must install and maintain an operable employee alarm system "unless employees can promptly see or smell a fire or other hazard in time to provide adequate warning to them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.37(b)(3) say about decorations and signs on an exit route door?

options.A: The door must be free of decorations or signs that obscure its visibility
options.B: Seasonal decorations are allowed if they are fire retardant
options.C: Any decoration is allowed if the exit sign above the door is lit
options.D: Decorations are allowed on the inside face of the door only

questions.explanation: The rule says "Each exit route door must be free of decorations or signs that obscure the visibility of the exit route door."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: If the direction of travel to the exit or exit discharge is not immediately apparent, what does 1910.37(b)(4) require?

options.A: A floor plan handed to each employee at hire
options.B: Signs posted along the exit access indicating the direction of travel to the nearest exit and exit discharge
options.C: A second exit door next to the first
options.D: An employee posted at each corner during an emergency

questions.explanation: In that case "signs must be posted along the exit access indicating the direction of travel to the nearest exit and exit discharge," and "the line-of-sight to an exit sign must clearly be visible at all times."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.38(e) require the employer to do so that an evacuation is safe and orderly?

options.A: Hire an outside evacuation company
options.B: Hold an evacuation drill every month
options.C: Designate and train employees to assist in a safe and orderly evacuation of other employees
options.D: Install a public address system on every floor

questions.explanation: Under the training paragraph, "An employer must designate and train employees to assist in a safe and orderly evacuation of other employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.38, Emergency action plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which is one of the times 1910.38(f) requires the employer to review the emergency action plan with a covered employee?

options.A: Only once every five years
options.B: Only after an OSHA inspection
options.C: Only when the employee asks
options.D: When the employee's responsibilities under the plan change

questions.explanation: The employer must review the plan with each covered employee "When the plan is developed or the employee is assigned initially to a job," "When the employee's responsibilities under the plan change," and "When the plan is changed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.38, Emergency action plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Employees may need more information about the emergency action plan or an explanation of their duties under it. What does 1910.38(c)(6) require the plan to include for this?

options.A: The name or job title of every employee who may be contacted by employees who need more information about the plan or an explanation of their duties under the plan
options.B: The telephone number of the nearest OSHA area office
options.C: The full text of 1910.38 printed at the front of the plan
options.D: Each employee's home telephone number

questions.explanation: One minimum element of the plan is "The name or job title of every employee who may be contacted by employees who need more information about the plan or an explanation of their duties under the plan."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.38, Emergency action plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which item must a fire prevention plan include under 1910.39(c)?

options.A: A list of employees' home phone numbers
options.B: Procedures to control accumulations of flammable and combustible waste materials
options.C: The workplace's fire insurance premium
options.D: A schedule of fire department social visits

questions.explanation: A fire prevention plan must include "Procedures to control accumulations of flammable and combustible waste materials."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.39, Fire prevention plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When must an employer inform employees of the fire hazards to which they are exposed?

options.A: Only after a fire has occurred
options.B: Only when an employee asks
options.C: Upon initial assignment to a job
options.D: Only when OSHA requests it

questions.explanation: "An employer must inform employees upon initial assignment to a job of the fire hazards to which they are exposed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.39, Fire prevention plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)
